header: Problem 10 Synthesis of Indigoid Compounds (25 points)

subquestions.text_open: 10-1 In 1909, H. Friedländer noted that an excellent purple pigment mentioned in the Bible—the pigment that the Romans called Tyrian purple after the Phoenician port of Tyre in present-day Lebanon—was in fact 6,6'-dibromoindigo, F. This precious early dye was extracted from small purple sea snails, the murex; as many as 12000 snails were required to prepare 1.5 g of dye. After nearly a century of continuing research into its synthesis, Pinkney and Chammers proposed a new method, which Iming and coworkers improved into an efficient route. 10-1-1 Give the SMILES of intermediate E.

text_images.description: 10-1 Synthetic route. This multistep scheme begins at the upper left with 'CC1=CC=C(N)C=C1', which reacts under HNO_3 and H_2SO_4 to give intermediate B. B reacts under 1) NaNO_2, HBr and 2) CuBr to give C. C then reacts under CrO_3 and (CH_3CO)_2O to give D. In the second row, D reacts under H_2SO_4 and H_2O to give E. Finally, E reacts under NaOH and H_2O, (CH_3)_2CO to give the product F at the lower right, with SMILES 'O=C1NC2=C(C=C(Br)C=C2)C1=C3NC4=C(C=C(Br)C=C4)C3=O'.

subquestions.text_open: 10-1-2 Explain the regioselectivity of the conversion of A into B. (No more than 50 words.)

10-2 In the route above, conversion of E into F is clearly the key step. In fact, as early as 1882, Baeyer used this reaction to synthesize indigo in one step from o-nitrobenzaldehyde. 10-2-1 Write the chemical equation for this reaction, representing o-nitrobenzaldehyde and indigo by their SMILES.

text_images.description: One-step synthesis. At the far left is 'O=CC1=CC=CC=C1[N+]([O-])=O', labeled G below. Under NaOH and H_2O, (CH_3)_2CO, it gives the product at the far right, 'O=C1NC(C=CC=C2)=C2/C1=C3NC4=C(C=CC=C4)C/3=O', labeled H below.

subquestions.text_open: 10-3 Nitrogen plays a key role in the reaction above, but analogous substrates and methods are unsuitable for obtaining the sulfur-substituted product. After the nineteen-eighties, Scottish chemists synthesized thioindigo, K, using the reaction below. The reaction still proceeds through an intermediate containing a fused six- and five-membered ring system. It is known that contraction of the six-membered ring into the five-membered ring does not occur by ring opening followed by ring closure. Answer the following questions. 10-3-1 In what form does the oxygen atom of the sulfoxide depart?

text_images.description: Structure/reaction description for synthesis of thioindigo K. Sulfoxide J gives thioindigo K under NaOAc/HOAc. The SMILES of J is 'BrC(C1=O)=C([S+](C2=C1C=CC=C2)[O-])Br'; thioindigo K may be represented as 'O=C1C2=C(S/C1=C3SC4=C(C\3=O)C=CC=C4)C=CC=C2'.
